prompt: This is an art-direction redesign for Yorimichi, a stylised Japanese autumn exploration game made in Unreal. Image 1 is a real, unretouched screenshot of the game as it is now. Repaint THE SAME VIEW from the same camera, keeping the layout, street grid, terrain, building positions, sea and sky composition, but redesigned to the standard of a polished commercial stylised game (think Ghibli-inspired, hand-crafted, cosy, dense and lived-in): textured materials with soft hand-painted detail instead of flat untextured colour, coherent warm autumn palette, gentle afternoon sunlight. It must stay a believable real-time game frame built from meshes, textures and foliage, not a loose illustration. No text, no UI, no watermark. Aerial over the autumn forest north of the city. The current trees are faceted low-poly icosphere blobs in flat colours. Redesign them as dense, lush stylised trees with soft clustered leaf canopies (like Ghibli or the exploration camera painterly foliage): many overlapping leaf clumps with soft shading, subsurface glow where the sun hits, dark gaps between crowns, mixed species (red and orange maples, yellow ginkgo and birch, deep green cedar and pine), natural density variation and clearings. Keep the trail and the terrain shape.
